scenes.heading: Solving exponential equations
scenes.sub: When the unknown is in the index
scenes.say: How many years until your savings double? How long until a medicine wears off? These questions lead to equations with the unknown up in the index. Here are three ways to solve them.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: Change both prices into the same currency before comparing
scenes.science: Change both sides into powers of the same base: 4ˣ = 8 → 2²ˣ = 2³
scenes.breaks: Exchange rates change daily, but 4 = 2² is exact forever.
scenes.say: You can't compare a price in dollars with a price in yen until you change them into the same currency. Exponential equations are the same. Four to the x equals eight is tricky, but write both sides as powers of two and you can just compare the indices.

scenes.heading: Method 1: same base
scenes.question: Solve 4ˣ = 8.
scenes.say: Solve four to the x equals eight. Four is two squared and eight is two cubed. So two to the two x equals two cubed. Same base, so the indices are equal: two x equals three, and x is three halves.
scenes.caption: Solve 4ˣ = 8. 4 is 2² and 8 is 2³. So 2²ˣ = 2³. Same base, so the indices are equal: 2x = 3, and x = 3/2.

scenes.heading: Method 2: logarithms
scenes.equation: aˣ = b  ⇒  x = log b ÷ log a
scenes.say: When the bases won't match, use logs. If a to the x equals b, then x equals log b divided by log a. For five to the x equals twenty, x is log twenty over log five, about one point eight six.
scenes.caption: When the bases won't match, use logs. If aˣ = b, then x = log b ÷ log a. For 5ˣ = 20, x = log 20 ÷ log 5 ≈ 1.86.

scenes.heading: Method 3: read the graph
notes: Draw y = 2ˣ and the line y = 10
Read down from where they meet
scenes.say: You can also use a graph. First the curve y equals two to the x. Then the line y equals ten. From where they meet, drop down to the x-axis: about three point three two. That is the solution of two to the x equals ten.
scenes.caption: You can also use a graph. First the curve y = 2ˣ. Then the line y = 10. From where they meet, drop down to the x-axis: about 3.32. That is the solution of 2ˣ = 10.

scenes.heading: How long to double?
scenes.question: $5000 at 6% p.a. compounded annually. When does it first double?
scenes.say: Five thousand dollars at six per cent a year. When does it double? Divide by five thousand: one point zero six to the n equals two. So n is log two over log one point zero six, about eleven point nine. It only gets there during year twelve, so round up: twelve years.
scenes.caption: $5000 at 6% a year. When does it double? Divide by 5000: 1.06ⁿ = 2. So n = log 2 ÷ log 1.06 ≈ 11.9. It only gets there during year 12, so round up: 12 years.

points: Same base → set the indices equal
Otherwise x = log b ÷ log a
Graph: x where y = aˣ meets y = b
scenes.say: Quick recap. If you can write both sides with the same base, set the indices equal. If not, x equals log b over log a. A graph gives a quick estimate. And for whole periods, round up. Now try the practice questions!
